Under the general direction of the Chief Psychologist in the Psychological Screening Program (PSP in the Medical and Psychological Screening Division) (MPSD) of [Company name masked], the Psychologist is responsible for applying psychological knowledge in a multi-step process to assess the psychological suitability of peace officer and non-peace officer candidates during the selection process. The Psychologist must conduct psychological suitability assessments using criteria set forth by the Peace Officer Standards and Training (POST) manual.
cond_0146.responsibilities:
You will find additional information about the job in the Duty Statement.
Special Requirements:
The position requires a Psychologist License. You will be required to provide a copy of your license prior to being hired.
You must submit a Statement of Qualifications (SOQ). You need to provide direct responses to each of the numbered items. You must include the numbered item followed by your response. Include specific examples of your education, training, and/or experience. Limit your SOQ to two (2) pages, single-spaced, twelve-point Arial font.
Describe how your professional experience will enable you to develop the necessary knowledge, skills, and abilities to effectively conduct preemployment psychological assessments of law enforcement candidates while working collaboratively as part of a team of psychologists. Please provide examples to illustrate your points. The Commission on Peace Officer Standards and Training requires peace officer candidates to be evaluated for explicit and implicit bias against race or ethnicity, gender, nationality, religion, disability, or sexual orientation. Explain your understanding of how this is relevant to public safety and public trust.

You will work closely with a team of psychologists, regularly communicating with colleagues and engaging with candidates throughout a multi-step assessment process. The role involves applying psychological knowledge to assess the suitability of peace officer and non-peace officer candidates during the selection process, using criteria set forth by the Peace Officer Standards and Training (POST) manual.
cond_0222.responsibilities:
Conduct psychological suitability assessments of peace officer and non-peace officer candidates using POST criteria
Administer and score written psychological tests measuring psychopathology, personality traits, and suitability for peace officer work
Conduct structured clinical interviews with candidates, actively engaging with each individual to gather relevant information
Review and incorporate information from collateral sources
Prepare, review, and edit written psychological reports
Communicate findings and explain assessment decisions clearly to colleagues and within the team
Stay in regular contact with team members to coordinate workload and maintain consistent standards
Conduct research to keep current knowledge of peace officer selection practices and related psychological concepts
Actively contribute to a collaborative team environment, raising questions and sharing observations with fellow psychologists
Travel as needed to attend meetings, trainings, or conferences
cond_0222.requirements:
A writing sample (redacted psychological report) is required. You must also submit a Statement of Qualifications (SOQ) of no more than two pages, single-spaced, twelve-point Arial font, with direct responses to each numbered item and specific examples of your education, training, and experience. A valid Psychologist License is required; you will need to provide a copy prior to being hired.
Minimum Requirements**
Knowledge of assessing written psychological tests to measure psychopathology, personality traits, and suitability for peace officer work
Knowledge of principles of conducting clinical structured psychological interviews
Knowledge of test construction and validation procedures
Knowledge of the application of screening methodology and procedures to specialized law enforcement populations
Ability to prepare, review, and edit written reports
Ability to review and incorporate information from collateral sources
Ability to present ideas clearly, logically, and persuasively, both orally and in writing
Ability to meet deadlines and manage time independently
Integrity, conscientiousness, and dependability
Emotional stability
Preferred Requirements**
Knowledge of the psychology of implicit bias
Ability to develop rapport with diverse individuals and engage comfortably across a range of backgrounds
Ability to initiate and maintain cooperative working relationships with colleagues and candidates
Ability to conduct research to stay current on relevant developments in peace officer selection
Demonstrated commitment to diversity and inclusion
Ability to leverage the creativity and perspective brought by a diverse workforce
Keenness of observation
Patience

Under the general direction of the Chief Psychologist in the Psychological Screening Program (PSP in the Medical and Psychological Screening Division) (MPSD) of [Company name masked], the Psychologist is responsible for applying psychological knowledge in a multi-step process to assess the psychological suitability of peace officer and non-peace officer candidates during the selection process. The Psychologist must conduct psychological suitability assessments using criteria set forth by the Peace Officer Standards and Training (POST) manual.
cond_0271.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Knowledge of assessing written psychological tests to measure psychopathology, personality traits, and suitability for peace officer work
Knowledge of principles of effectively conducting clinical structured psychological interviews
Knowledge of test construction and validation procedures
Knowledge of the application of screening methodology and procedures to specialized law enforcement populations
Knowledge of the psychology of implicit bias
Ability to prepare, review, and edit written reports
Ability to review and incorporate information from collateral sources
Ability to present ideas clearly, logically, and persuasively, both orally and in writing
Ability to establish and maintain cooperative working relationships
Ability to manage time and prioritize workload independently
Ability to meet deadlines
Integrity, conscientiousness, and dependability
Emotional stability
Preferred Requirements
Ability to conduct research to maintain current knowledge of relevant information related to the practice of peace officer selection and related psychological concepts
Ability to leverage the power and creativity brought about by a diverse workforce to improve the division and department

Demonstrated commitment to diversity and inclusion

cond_0367.intro:
The Medical and Psychological Screening Division (MPSD) at [Company name masked] is looking for an experienced Psychologist to conduct preemployment psychological evaluations of peace officer candidates.
Under the general direction of the Chief Psychologist in the Psychological Screening Program (PSP), the Psychologist applies psychological knowledge in a multi-step process to assess the psychological suitability of peace officer and non-peace officer candidates during the selection process. Assessments must follow criteria set forth by the Peace Officer Standards and Training (POST) manual.
cond_0367.responsibilities:
Conduct preemployment psychological suitability assessments of peace officer and non-peace officer candidates using POST-mandated criteria.
Administer and score written psychological tests measuring psychopathology, personality traits, and suitability for peace officer work.
Conduct structured clinical psychological interviews as part of the assessment process.
Review and incorporate information from collateral sources into assessment conclusions.
Prepare, review, and edit written psychological reports documenting assessment findings.
Document findings and share them with relevant team members and supervisors as required.
Maintain current knowledge of peace officer selection practices and relevant psychological concepts through independent research.
Coordinate with the team of psychologists on case-related tasks and procedural matters.
Manage workload independently to meet assessment deadlines.
cond_0367.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Valid Psychologist license (copy required prior to hire)
Knowledge of written psychological tests used to measure psychopathology, personality traits, and peace officer suitability
Knowledge of principles of conducting structured clinical psychological interviews
Knowledge of test construction and validation procedures
Knowledge of screening methodology and procedures applied to law enforcement populations
Ability to prepare, review, and edit written reports
Ability to review and incorporate information from collateral sources
Ability to manage time and prioritize workload independently and meet deadlines
Integrity, conscientiousness, and dependability
Emotional stability and patience
Keenness of observation
Preferred Requirements
Knowledge of the psychology of implicit bias
Ability to present ideas clearly, logically, and directly, both in writing and verbally
Ability to establish and maintain cooperative working relationships
Ability to conduct research to stay current on peace officer selection and related psychological concepts
Ability to develop rapport with diverse individuals
Demonstrated commitment to diversity and inclusion
Ability to contribute to a diverse workforce to improve division outcomes
